title: Is the Shannon capacity of a finite graph computable?
formal: Is there an algorithm that, given a finite graph G and a positive integer k, outputs a rational number within 2^(−k) of Θ(G), where Θ(G)=sup over m≥1 of α(G strong-power m)^(1/m)?
context:
This fixes computability rather than promising a particular running time. The exact value for C7 is a separate question.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Asks whether a finite zero-error communication model has an effectively approximable asymptotic information rate.
